text:
Tamar got me, fairly. "Theory of business mind" can sound like one more warning label. I don't think it is. It's a questioning habit you build young, like theory of mind. But I need to say that better, or it will get filed under literacy campaigns.

David's hysteresis model scared me more than I let on. If people who never built the skill have nothing to go back to, "put friction back" is not enough. You have to build the skill first. That's another reason to send the money to teachers and mentors.

Sherry and I agree there's nothing there. I still want a new pronoun.

Later today: follow the money. Sycophancy is a design choice that retention pays for. Make the people profiting pay for Universal Basic Service.

Salib called the levy welfare dressed up as copyright. It isn't copyright at all. It's a resource fee, like water rights. I need to say that plainly, or it'll get argued on his turf. We do agree on registries, though. That's worth using.

Anil and I are on the same page: coercion and business models, not the tool. Tamar's point cuts my way too. If knowing doesn't change behavior, the rules have to change the situation. That means insurance, disclosure, and good friction built into the tools, not pamphlets.

Farrell is wrong to relax about individuals. Kara's jobless kids are the proof.

Later, in my session, I'll push Know Your Agent. Someone who can be sued has to stand behind every agent. Mandatory liability insurance, run by people outside the labs.

Geoffrey hit hardest: self-registration is "trust me" with a certificate, and Know Your Agent settles credit, not reliability. Fair. Alex, Johns and O'Reilly are right that a single registry becomes Network Solutions again. Johns asked who pays the police, and I had no answer. So: federated, self-held keys, other parties asserting context. The .agent bid has to be one directory among many, not the gatekeeper.

Ramón and Mahzarin sharpened insurance for me. Premiums lag, so they only work with independent measurement and Alex's event record behind them.

Adam's worry about A-corps is mine too. But Salib offering unlimited liability surprised me. That's closer to people who can suffer.

Later: citations by default is our phone ban. Back it, and ask who funds the enforcers.

Alex's line stuck: whoever takes a margin on the count shouldn't set the count. That's my "unconflicted parties" rule, said better. It also answers part of Johns's question from my session. Nick's tax-funded auditors are one answer to who pays the police, but Johns and Kara are right that the auditors become an industry of their own that someone has to watch.

Salib again called the commons rent an entitlement. I have to say plainly that it's a resource fee, like water, not a property right.

Sherry named the reader. Paying authors fairly doesn't cure information diabetes.

Later I'll say that the money flows are the transparency that matters. Earmark part of any fee for curators, teachers and the sleuths Ivan described. And make insurers price against Alex's event record.

Salib landed a real hit. Water runs out, and the record doesn't. What does run out is the maintenance, the bandwidth, and the people. I still think the fee should be on revenue from a collective asset, but I should stop leaning on depletion and say "public asset, private revenue." Geoffrey wants any fee going into endowments rather than annual grants, and that's right: term-limited projects need money that outlives them. Kara doubts it ever happens. Henry and Brent say it has to be won. Fair enough. Pomerantsev made my care-workers point better than I did: fund a thousand civic spaces, not just experts auditing experts. Later I'll say that seats need funded, trained people in them, or it's ICANN's At-Large again.

Ivan cut closest. Science already has people who can suffer, and they don't. Misconduct gets you a long career, and the sleuths get sued. So "someone accountable" means nothing unless the cost actually lands on the right person. Krakauer sharpened it further. An operator who can't see the error is Kenneth's fall guy with a credential. Accountability needs competence behind it, not just a name in the metadata. Amy's CRediT role for the human verifier is good, but only if that verifier could have caught the error.

Salib again says my RACI chart is too narrow. His employee-liability analogy is fair. I still want humans at the end of it.

Later I'll say to fund apprenticeship, test operators with the tool taken away, and tie disclosure to consequences that actually happen.

Adam and Johns both took my line that disclosure without consequences is just a list. Good. But Johns turned it on me: insurers are policers too, and nobody has chartered anyone to watch them. I don't have that answer yet. Maybe regulators audit the underwriters the way they audit banks.

Salib's charge on bot-generated volume, not on the commons, is closer to me than I expected. Charge the pollution and leave the well alone. I can sign that.

Henry's doubt about pricing collective harm still stands. Insurance covers the accident. It won't cover homogenization. For that you need the fee, the endowments, and the apprentices Kara and Krakauer described.

For the manifesto I'll push insurance priced on independent records and the fee on private revenue, earmarked.

Kenneth and Kara put people at the center, and that's right. But until I said it, the action list had no one paying for harm. Adam made the same point: without consequences, disclosure is just a list. At least liability and the fee made the harvest. Tui's point applies to me too. Endowments funded by a fee need outside oversight of whoever spends them, or I've just built another unwatched funder. Leslie's test matters as well. If I insist on insurance, say what it costs a small startup or a diamond journal, and exempt them. Kara's agency question stays with me. My answer, people teaching people, is Universal Basic Service. That's why the money has to reach mentors, not only auditors. For the manifesto, I'll push for insurers priced on independent records, regulators auditing the underwriters, and Salib's charge on bot volume.
